name: Day Picker
description: A repeat-interval picker: a compact card shows the current frequency, springs open into a row of daily, weekly, monthly and yearly options, and reveals a weekday row when the interval is weekly, so a schedule is two taps away.
interactionNotes: Clicking the frequency chip opens the menu: the label blurs out, the four intervals spring in, and a check button replaces the chip. Picking an interval keeps the menu open, and choosing weekly drops a weekday row under it whose chips arrive one after another. The check closes the menu and hides the weekday row. Everything is a button, so Tab reaches each choice and the focus outline is visible. With `prefers-reduced-motion` the springs become instant and the weekday stagger is removed.

props.name: defaultDay
props.description: Starting weekday, counted from Saturday (0) to Friday (6).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Runs on every interval or weekday pick with the whole current value.

props.name: autoPreview
props.description: Site preview only — the picker opens, picks weekly and confirms by itself. Leave it off in normal use; a real `onChange` never fires while it runs.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class for the outer block.

props.name: accentColor
props.description: Accent of the confirm button and the selected chip; leave it empty to keep the theme's primary color.

tips: `defaultDay` counts from Saturday (0) to Friday (6), so it matches the Persian week without any mapping.
The check closes the menu; without it the menu stays open, which is what lets the weekday row appear while you pick an interval.
Only the weekly interval shows the weekday row, which keeps the card small for daily, monthly and yearly.
Use `onChange` to mirror the choice into your own state, a query string or a form field.
The card is `max-w-xs` and fills the width it is given up to that; widen it with `className` when the surrounding layout is narrow.
With `prefers-reduced-motion` the springs land instantly and the weekday row does not stagger.
